title: Threat Detection Library - Windows Privileged Admin Action Validation Entry
description: Schema for a single entry in data/windows-privileged-admin-validations.json -- this library's fifth validation catalogue, alongside RHEL, FortiGate, Cisco SD-WAN, and RHEL IdM/IPA. Not a production detection rule: its 'search' field is a one-shot presence check ('did the expected event show up'), and its distinguishing fields (safe_test, test_step, rollback_step, test_result) describe executing an action once against a controlled Windows host and confirming the telemetry/detection fired. See docs/validations.md for the full rationale.

id.description: Stable catalogue identifier, sourced from the original workbook's Event ID column.

platform.description: Platform(s) this validation applies to. Every entry in this catalogue is Windows-endpoint-scoped today -- the exact same string data/windows-endpoint-detections.json's component enum already uses for this same generic Windows OS endpoint telemetry domain.

category.description: Original test grouping, e.g. User, Service, Registry, RDP, Defender, BitLocker.

event_type.description: High-level privileged activity taxonomy, e.g. Account management, Service management, Registry modification.

title.description: Canonical description of the privileged action.

description.description: Human-readable explanation of the action (the workbook's Examples column).

typical_mechanism.description: Common PowerShell cmdlet, net/sc/reg command, or GUI mechanism.

privilege_level.description: Expected privilege context, e.g. Administrative or delegated privilege.

mitre_attack.description: Resolved against the live MITRE ATT&CK STIX corpus at conversion time -- not copied verbatim from the workbook's ATT&CK Tactic column, which still used the pre-split 'Defense Evasion' tactic name, and not from its ATT&CK Technique column, some of whose values cited a revoked/renumbered technique ID (T1060, T1070.001, T1562.001, T1562.002, T1562.004) redirected via MITRE's own revoked-by relationship. A few rows cite two technique IDs in one cell; each is resolved independently and deduped by its current resolved ID (an old-ID/new-ID pair for the same technique collapses to one entry; two IDs that revoke to two different current techniques stay two). A minority of entries (those with no technique to anchor a lookup) may have an empty tactics/techniques array rather than a guessed mapping.

note.description: Optional context note from the source workbook, e.g. 'context dependent' or a MITRE renumbering redirect.

primary_telemetry.description: Primary Windows telemetry expected to record the action.

primary_windows_event_ids.description: Primary Windows Event ID(s) expected, e.g. ['4720'].

primary_channel.description: Primary Windows Event Log channel, e.g. 'Security', 'Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational'.

primary_provider.description: Primary Windows Event Log provider, e.g. 'Microsoft-Windows-Security-Auditing'.

safe_test.description: Whether this action is suitable for controlled testing without intentional disruptive impact.

test_step.description: Command or action used to generate the event.

test_result.description: Pass/Fail/Partial/Not Tested tracking field -- set by whoever actually runs the validation, not by this library.

expected_logon_type.description: Expected Windows logon type where applicable, e.g. '3 (network)', '10 (RemoteInteractive)'.

expected_target_account_object.description: Expected target account/object of the action.

expected_process_image.description: Expected process/image name generating the event, e.g. 'powershell.exe'.

expected_object_path.description: Expected registry key, scheduled task, service path, or file path touched by the action.

expected_command_line.description: Expected command line recorded in telemetry.

expected_fields.description: Minimum fields useful for validation and detection.

validation_spl.description: Starter SPL to validate event presence in Splunk -- a presence check, not a tuned detection rule.
